# Verdict v1.2 — generated by scripts/verdict.py (E021, revised E028). Do not edit by hand.

Metric: lifecycle launched kg per continuous kW of AI load, whole launches over L = 10/15/20 y (docs/PREREGISTRATION.md; D17 correction). B/C use choices FAVOURABLE to them (no bus/structure mass, optimal receiver spacing, dawn-dusk sunlight, full-sun ground PV). Each B/C tier is compared with the SAME A tier; A has no demonstrated next-tier value, so A-next = A-current.

## Branch A — GPUs in orbit
- current: 13.3–19.0 kg/kW per launch; life 5.0 y → L=10: **26.7–38.1**; L=15: **40.0–57.1**; L=20: **53.3–76.2** kg/kW (R1-005,R1-012,R1-023)
- speculative: 10.0–14.3 kg/kW per launch; life 5.0 y → L=10: **20.0–28.6**; L=15: **30.0–42.9**; L=20: **40.0–57.1** kg/kW (R1-020)

**Transmitter alone (weightless PV, duty 1), current tier: 92 kg/kW per launch** (277 over 15 y vs A 40) → B-LEO cannot beat A at today's measured transmitter specific power (28 W/kg RF-out, R2-043) whatever the solar array weighs.
Break-even transmitter specific power (weightless PV, duty 1, current chain): **194 W/kg RF-out** (6.9× today).
At the tier-baseline array (88.2 W/kg) the PV alone is 278 kg/kW over 15 y (duty 1) > A 40: **no transmitter value, however light, flips current-tier B-LEO** (preregistered single-parameter break-even: none).

## Branch C — orbital mirror → ground PV (625 km, 30° mask, zenith atmosphere 0.64, 45° tilt)
Mirror life 1 y: the only sourced life for an orbital reflector (Earendil-1 filing: ~1 y of operations, passive drag deorbit ~5 months, R1-115/116) → 15 launches over 15 y. Lighter reflectors (higher area-to-mass) decay faster, so the same life is applied to every tier; the break-even life is reported instead of assumed.

The fully covered receiver converts every watt of mirror light landing on the lit area at 30% (FAVOURABLE); a real tracking farm holds 59.3 MW_DC per km² at 1,000 W/m² (R5-077), i.e. about 5.9% of the light landing on its site (E034).
Tier provenance: current = Reflect's Earendil-1 as FILED with the FCC, 142 kg / 324 m² (R1-112/113; no flight in the ledger; filed orbit 88° inclination, 11:00 MLTAN (R1-114), whereas this model grants it dawn-dusk geometry — FAVOURABLE); next = NASA ACS3, the flown solar-SAIL spacecraft, ~16 kg / 80 m² (R1-151) — its optical figure and pointing as a sunlight relay are undemonstrated (ASSUMPTION); speculative = ACS3 membrane + booms only, no deployer or bus (R1-149/150).

**Minimum site scale (the mass rows assume it).** Ground PV produces nothing below the inverter start: 2.6 W/m² with an ideal module, ~5 W/m² at 50% low-light efficiency (R5-069). Over a ~26.5 km² zenith spot that needs 0.12–0.24 km² of mirror overhead AT ONCE (≈ 384–738 Earendil-1s per site), before any power flows. The per-kW mass above is valid only for constellations large enough to hold that density over every served site; below it the delivered power is zero.

Weather (clear-sky fraction): 0.66 all-hours and 0.62 night means of 12 utility-PV regions (R12-016, range 0.44–0.84); 0.33 global (MODIS ~67% cloud, R10-052) for coverage that is not limited to desert sites. 'Land-only' divides by the land fraction 0.291 (R12-019) — approximate, since coastal receivers also see some passes over the ocean.

## V3 — launch cost alone per MWh of AI (IT) electricity vs near-firm terrestrial solar
Terrestrial comparator: solar + battery sized for flat output 97% / 99.4% of hours, Las Vegas, modelled with 2024 global prices: $104 / $167 per delivered MWh (Ember, R5-027/028, STUDY-ASSUMED) → × PUE 1.15 = $120–192 per IT-MWh. It does not cover the remaining 0.6–3% of hours (their supply cost is not in the ledger). ## V4 — photonic compute (full system, matched precision)
No full-system photonic measurement at precision matched to B300 exists in the ledger. The only measured full-stack photonic AI processor reaches 0.81 TOPS/W ≈ 2.5 pJ/MAC average (R3-043; precision not matched) vs B300 chip level 0.19–0.56 pJ/MAC (R3-070) → **V4: not supported at the current tier.** Next/speculative: open — the quantities that decide it are P7 (support overhead), P8 (a measured wall-plug J/MAC) and P10 (precision equivalence) in docs/generated/open_problems.md.
